messages.subject: Problems of analysis of dung densities
parts:
Dear Fellow distance maillisters,
Let me begin by intorducing myself. My name is Amirtharaj Christy
Williams and I am doing my Ph.D. on elephants in a National Park in
north India. As a part of my work I have been doing transects to
estimate elephant dung densities in a very hilly terrain. Therefore, it
has not been always possible to lay a perfectly straight line transect.
Sometimes we do rock climbing on steep slopes (slight exagerration
should be forgiven) when we are doing the transects. Because dung piles
are immovable object the question of recounting does not arise. We also
have exact distance to the dung piles from the center of the line to
each dung pile. The questions I have are;
1. Will densities calculated from such transects be valid?

2. Has any simulation study been done comparing curvilinear with
straight line transects?

3. I have problem in running the Distance dos version in batch mode on
transect replicates which do not have any dung piles. The error message
I get is 'unexpected end of data encountered" and the program exits.

I would be much obliged to hear your feedbacks on this.

regards and thanks for your valuable time,
A. Christy Williams

messages.author: a52219e2e622d1af
messages.subject: Re: Problems of analysis of dung densities
parts:
> > 1. Will densities calculated from such transects be valid?

Possibly, provided they are representative on the ground in general. If
you systematically avoid steep slopes, and the elephants do too, you will
overestimate numbers.

> > 2. Has any simulation study been done comparing curvilinear with
> > straight line transects?

I don't know - but curved lines are perfectly OK if they're random ...
your problem is that both you and the elephants may find the flatter
terrain easier, so you may oversample areas preferentially used by the
elephants.

> > 3. I have problem in running the Distance dos version in batch mode on
> > transect replicates which do not have any dung piles. The error message
> > I get is 'unexpected end of data encountered" and the program exits.

I suggest you switch to the windows version - available free from the www
site below. The Dos version works fine though ... you're probably missing
a ';':

sample/label='line 1'/effort=1.2;
;
sample ...

is the format needed ... note the ';' on the second line.

Steve Buckland
